statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-114149 (GHSA-x33c-w48q-qrgc) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service: multipart form processing can bypass the configured header-count limit and consume excessive resources. Microsoft fixed it in ASP.NET Core 10.0.15 and lists the ASP.NET Core runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, and the standalone Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities package from 10.0.0 through 10.0.14 as affected (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-x33c-w48q-qrgc, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/511, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.15/10.0.15.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 10.0.15-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.115 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.115). Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside their nupkg and tar.gz archives: every build ships Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities.dll from its own .NET release, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore10-runtime and in the SDK, runtime-pack nupkg and ASP.NET Core runtime archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and dotnet10-runtime-artifacts also carries a Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities NuGet package of the same version; the earlier builds carry 10.0.2 through 10.0.14 and 10.0.15-r0 carries 10.0.15 on both architectures. The range ends at 10.0.15-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-114149 (GHSA-x33c-w48q-qrgc) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service: multipart form processing counted distinct header names rather than header lines against the configured header-count limit, so repeated headers in a section could bypass it and consume excessive resources. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 8.0 runtime, including the linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64 runtime packs, and Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities as affected up to 8.0.33 and fixed in 8.0.34, with the fix in MultipartReader (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-x33c-w48q-qrgc, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/e2fdf87f23ce5747bce1ac9a8c34905b17799a68, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.34/8.0.34.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET version it carries; its published builds are 8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0. We unpacked every package of 8.0.34-r0 for x86_64 and aarch64 (11 per architecture), including the nupkg and other archives inside them: every Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities.dll for .NET 8 (the shared framework in aspnetcore8-runtime, the .NET SDK and runtime pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, the standalone NuGet package and the reference packs in dotnet8-runtime-artifacts and aspnetcore8-targeting-pack) reports ASP.NET Core 8.0.34, built from the v8.0.34 source that includes the fix; the only other copy is a reference assembly in a source-build reference package for ASP.NET Core 6.0.2, which holds API signatures and no implementation code. The earlier builds carry ASP.NET Core 8.0.33 or older. The range ends at 8.0.34-r0, the first published build with the fix.

Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0 through 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities.dll from its own .NET release, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore9-runtime, in the reference pack of aspnetcore9-targeting-pack, in the shared framework, reference pack and ASP.NET Core runtime pack NuGet package held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap, and in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities and Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref NuGet packages held by dotnet9-runtime-artifacts; the earlier builds carry 9.0.12 through 9.0.22 and 9.0.23-r0 carries 9.0.23 on both architectures. The older Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref 6.0.2 and 8.0.0 packages that dotnet9-runtime-artifacts carries for source-build hold reference assemblies only, with no implementation code. CVE-2026-114149 (GHSA-x33c-w48q-qrgc): ASP.NET Core multipart form processing can bypass the configured header-count limit and consume excessive resources. Microsoft fixed it in ASP.NET Core 10.0.15 and Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities 10.0.15; 10.0 versions up to 10.0.14 are affected (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-x33c-w48q-qrgc, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/511). The fix, "Correctly limit multipart header count" in the multipart reader of Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities, is commit bf1ee423d199a65f259dbc56c1e69b9f87bbde28 on the dotnet/dotnet release/10.0.1xx branch, from which the .NET 10 runtime and ASP.NET Core shared framework are built (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/bf1ee423d199a65f259dbc56c1e69b9f87bbde28); it is contained in the v10.0.15 tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.15) and not in v10.0.14. DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK. Unpacked every published dotnet-sdk-10 package in the DHI Debian repository, 10 builds from 10.0.301-0 to the current 10.0.404-1 for amd64 and arm64, each verified against the repository index checksum, including the .nupkg and .zip archives inside them, and read the file and product version of every copy of Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities.dll; both architectures agree in every build. Each build carries a copy in the ASP.NET Core shared framework (shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App) and a reference assembly in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref targeting pack, and in each build every copy has the same version as the ASP.NET Core shared framework it belongs to: 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0, and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1. The 10.0.15 copies record source commit 8e0f8ed2312954727f8919d7d1c2f78b483b4ee7, which contains the fix commit; the 10.0.14 copies record 0427b9abbead3fa64c6655eb4290c537397131fa, which does not. No .nupkg or .zip archive in these packages contains the assembly. The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages from the same source, 10.0.301-0 to 10.0.404-1, hold only a configuration file and a changelog. So 10.0.404-0, the first build of SDK 10.0.404 and of ASP.NET Core 10.0.15, is the first fixed build, and every earlier build carries ASP.NET Core 10.0.9 to 10.0.14. The range ends at 10.0.404-0.

CVE-2026-114149 (GHSA-x33c-w48q-qrgc): ASP.NET Core multipart form processing can bypass the configured header-count limit and consume excessive resources. Microsoft fixed it in ASP.NET Core 10.0.15 and Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities 10.0.15; 10.0 versions up to 10.0.14 are affected (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-x33c-w48q-qrgc, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/511). The fix, "Correctly limit multipart header count" in the multipart reader of Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities, is commit bf1ee423d199a65f259dbc56c1e69b9f87bbde28 on the dotnet/dotnet release/10.0.1xx branch, from which the .NET 10 runtime and ASP.NET Core shared framework are built (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/bf1ee423d199a65f259dbc56c1e69b9f87bbde28); it is contained in the v10.0.15 tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.15) and not in v10.0.14. DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK. Unpacked every published dotnet-sdk-10 package in the DHI Debian repository, 10 builds from 10.0.301-0 to the current 10.0.404-1 for amd64 and arm64, each verified against the repository index checksum, including the .nupkg and .zip archives inside them, and read the file and product version of every copy of Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities.dll; both architectures agree in every build. Each build carries a copy in the ASP.NET Core shared framework (shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App) and a reference assembly in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref targeting pack, and in each build every copy has the same version as the ASP.NET Core shared framework it belongs to: 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0, and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1. The 10.0.15 copies record source commit 8e0f8ed2312954727f8919d7d1c2f78b483b4ee7, which contains the fix commit; the 10.0.14 copies record 0427b9abbead3fa64c6655eb4290c537397131fa, which does not. No .nupkg or .zip archive in these packages contains the assembly. The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages from the same source, 10.0.301-0 to 10.0.404-1, hold only a configuration file and a changelog. So 10.0.404-0, the first build of SDK 10.0.404 and of ASP.NET Core 10.0.15, is the first fixed build, and every earlier build carries ASP.NET Core 10.0.9 to 10.0.14. The range ends at 10.0.404-0.
